transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep forgetting things that I really shouldn't. Important things, you know? Like my heart follow-up appointments, or remembering to actually call the clinic back. And it's everyday stuff, too—I'll go to start a repair job around the house and realize I showed up without the right tools. It's happening a lot, and I just need to figure out what's going on.
Is this memory problem a change from how you used to be?

Yeah, it is a change. I mean, it's been causing real trouble for... I'd say about a year and two months now. 

It really started right after I had a cardiac scare. Because of that, I had to cut way back on all the walking and the different projects I usually do. And, well, those things used to keep me settled, you know? Since I had to stop doing as much of that, it just seems like I can't keep track of anything anymore.
Besides forgetting things, have you had trouble managing your bills or finances?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues there. I'm still paying everything on time and keeping track of the checkbook just fine. It really is just... well, like I said, the appointments and the everyday things around the house. The money side of things hasn't been a problem.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

No, I haven't really been feeling down or depressed. I mean, it's frustrating not being able to do as much as I used to, physically, but my mood itself has been okay. I'm not feeling sad or anything like that. Just... scattered.
Have you been feeling unusually worried or anxious lately?

No, not really. I mean, I worry a bit about my health since the heart scare, which I think is pretty normal, but I wouldn't say I'm unusually anxious or stressed out. I'm just mostly frustrated with my memory and not being able to burn off my energy like I used to. But no real anxiety, no.
Before these memory problems started, did you have a stroke, head injury, or any other problem affecting your brain?

No, nothing like that. I've never had a stroke or a head injury... or anything else wrong with my brain, really. Like I said, I had that heart scare a while back, but as far as physical damage to my head goes, no, nothing at all.
Did a doctor ever tell you that your memory problems are related to a medical condition?

No, no doctor has ever said that. They haven't tied the memory stuff to any specific medical condition. I mean, I've brought it up before, but they never told me it was because of a disease or anything like that.
Because of your memory problems, do you need help with your usual day-to-day tasks?

No, I don't need any help. I can still handle all my usual day-to-day stuff just fine. I mean, I might forget where I put my keys or lose track of what I went into a room for, but I can still take care of myself, pay my bills, do the grocery shopping... all of that. I don't need anyone looking after me.
Have you ever had memory testing that showed a problem?
No, I haven't. I've never actually taken any kind of official memory test or anything, so... no, nothing like that has ever shown a problem.
Did your memory problems begin after a doctor started you on a new heart medication?
No, I haven't started any new heart medication. So, uh, no, it definitely didn't begin because of anything like that.
Has any doctor diagnosed you with a medical illness that affects your brain or memory?
No, never. I haven't been diagnosed with anything like that. No doctor has ever told me I have a disease or an illness that messes with my brain or my memory. So, no.
Has anyone close to you noticed that your memory has gotten worse?
No, not at all. Uh, nobody in my family has ever said anything about my memory slipping. So, no, I don't think anyone close to me has noticed it getting worse or anything like that.
Would it be okay if I do a brief memory test with you right now?
Yeah, that's fine. I don't mind doing a test right now. Go right ahead.
Please repeat these three words after me: apple, table, penny.
Okay. Apple, table, penny.
What were the three words I asked you to remember?
Apple, table, and penny.
Has a family member or close friend told you that your memory has been getting worse?
No, no one's said anything like that to me. My memory seems just fine as far as I know.
Has a doctor ever told you that your memory problems are more than what would be expected from normal aging?
No, never. Like I said, I haven't really had any memory problems to begin with, so no doctor has ever mentioned anything like that to me.
Have you ever had any medical test or brain scan that showed a problem affecting your memory or thinking?
No, I haven't. I've never had a brain scan or any kind of test for my memory. There's just been no reason to.
Has any doctor ever told you that your heart problem caused damage to your brain or affected your memory?
No, no doctor has ever told me that. I don't really have any heart problems to begin with, so... yeah, definitely nothing about it damaging my brain or affecting my memory.
